definitions: an adult female human being:
an adult who lives and identifies as female though they may have been considered to have a different sex at birth :
a wife or female sexual partner :
women in general :
used to form nouns describing certain types of women or women with certain jobs :
examples: She's a really nice woman.
A woman and two men were arrested the day after the explosion .
Women first got the vote in Britain in 1918.
She is Ireland's first woman (= female )
Mary is a woman who was assigned male at birth .
Marie is a transgender woman (= she was considered to be male at birth )

definitions: members of the working class (= a social group that consists of people who own little or no property and who have to work , usually doing physical work , to get money ) :
examples: He preached to anyone who would listen that the workers of the world were being abused by the wealthy .
He firmly believed that the workers would rise again.
A workers' revolt later that year forced the issue .
He spent his life defending the rights of the workers.

definitions: plural of woman
pl of woman
types of behaviour :
(used in adverbs ) in the stated direction or manner :
examples: Over the years we've got used to his funny little ways.
He's always been lazy and I don't think he's going to change his ways now.
When I moved to the commune , I found their ways very strange .
She grew tired of having to explain her family's ways to others .
If you're not careful , you'll soon slip back into your old ways.

definitions: a building or room where people perform their jobs , or these places generally :
a place where people do their jobs
examples: The survey asks workers about facilities in their workplace.
There can be no doubt that health and safety standards in the workplace have increased significantly since the introduction of the law .
We are trying to eliminate sex discrimination in the workplace .
In the new digital workplace, employers are finding it difficult to recruit individuals with experience in growing e-businesses.
workplace bullying / injuries / violence
in the workplace There can be no doubt that health and safety standards in the workplace have increased significantly since the introduction of the law .

definitions: everything that you might want or expect to find in a particular situation :
an industrial building , especially one where a lot of people are employed :
the parts of a machine , especially those that move :
all the extra things that may be offered with something:
the parts of a machine , esp . the parts that move
examples: The bridegroom was wearing a morning suit , gloves , top hat - the works .
And can I have two large pizzas with the works (= with all available types of food on top )
We both had starters , a main course , and a dessert - the works !
I had a facial , a massage , my eyebrows fixed , my nails done - the works .
It was a super-expensive hotel with the whole works : a swimming pool , gym , steam and sauna room , tennis courts .
a steel / iron works

definitions: a type of thin book with large pages and a paper cover that contains articles and photographs about subjects that are believed to be interesting for women, such as fashion , food , and health :
examples: She has written articles for several women's magazines .
I got a job as the fashion editor of a woman's magazine .

definitions: not correct :
If someone is wrong, they are not correct in their judgment or statement about something:
to show by your actions that someone's judgment of you was not correct :
not suitable or correct , or not as it should be:
Something that is wrong is not considered to be socially acceptable or suitable :
examples: Three of your answers were wrong.
That clock is wrong - it's 12.30, not 12.15.
Some of his facts are questionable , others are plainly (= completely )
You were wrong about the time - the bank closed at 3.30.
He's wrong in thinking that we will support the project financially .
I thought she couldn't do it, but she proved me wrong.

definitions: a clear liquid , without colour or taste , that falls from the sky as rain and is necessary for animal and plant life :
an area of water, such as the sea , a lake , or a swimming pool :
the level of an area of water:
a way of referring to urine (= yellowish liquid waste from the body ) :
the area of sea near to and belonging to a particular country :
examples: a bottle / drink / glass of water
bottled / mineral / tap water
hot / cold water
Can I have a drop of water in my whisky , please ?
Is there enough hot water for a bath ?
The human body is about 50 percent water.

definitions: inside or not further than an area or period of time :
inside the limits of something, for example the law or a set of rules , and allowed by it:
inside or not beyond (a particular area , limit , or period of time ):
examples: Two thirds of Californians live within 15 miles of the coast .
In 1992 cross-border controls within the EU were dismantled .
For orders within the UK, please enclose £2.50 for post and packing .
The resort lies within easy reach of (= not far from)
We recommend that this wine should be consumed within six months .
Within hours of the tragedy happening , an emergency rescue team had been assembled .

definitions: the money earned by an employee , esp . when paid for the hours worked :
examples: He was notorious for being anti-union and for paying low wages.

definitions: used to refer to plants or animals that live or grow independently of people , in natural conditions and with natural characteristics :
Wild land is not used to grow crops and has few people living in it:
uncontrolled , violent , or extreme :
very unusual , often in a way that is attractive or exciting :
not based on facts and is probably wrong :
examples: A wild animal such as a bear would not be happy living in a cage .
These herbs grow wild in the area .
wild grasses
a herd of wild horses
This part of the country is a wild, mountainous region .
The audience burst into wild applause .

definitions: an unnecessary or wrong use of money , substances , time , energy , abilities , etc.:
to not be used, eaten , etc.:
unwanted matter or material of any type , especially what is left after useful substances or parts have been removed :
an area of ground in or near a city that is not built on or used in any way:
large areas of land that are not used to grow crops and have few living animals or plants :
examples: That meeting achieved absolutely nothing - it was a complete waste of time .
She's been unemployed for two years and it's such a waste of her talents .
My mother couldn't stand waste - she always made us eat everything on our plates .
You can even make stock from the bones , so that nothing goes to waste.
Each year , the leftover flu vaccine goes to waste.
It's not fair to say that all the money and hard work went to waste.
